criteria.title: Scope: locations, matching, live trip, payment

levels.0: Lists 'request a ride and pay' only, or designs shared rides, ratings and onboarding unasked.
levels.1: Covers location tracking, matching and trips, but treats payment or the trip lifecycle as an afterthought.
levels.2: Covers drivers streaming location, nearby cars with fare estimates, request and offer/accept, live trip with ETAs, guarded lifecycle including cancellation, and end-of-trip charging; surge at awareness level; shared and scheduled rides out of scope.

levels.1: States match time and availability, but not the no-double-assignment or exactly-once charging guarantees.
levels.2: Match within 10 s, a driver never on two trips, exactly-once charging, positions a few seconds fresh, and explicitly best-effort durability for location updates; the two halves (firehose vs transaction) named as having different guarantees.

levels.0: No numbers, or numbers without derivation.
levels.1: Derives 250,000 updates/s but not trip writes, searches or concurrent trips.
levels.2: 1M ÷ 4 s = 250,000 updates/s (25 MB/s), 231 trips/s (463 peak), about 3,240 trip writes/s at peak, about 24,500 searches/s, 555,600 concurrent trips, and the conclusion that 98% of writes are disposable while the critical writes fit on one primary.

levels.0: Ignores the maps and payment providers' limits.
levels.1: Mentions the limits without computing usage.
levels.2: Adds up maps calls (estimates, dispatch matrices, ETA refreshes ≈ 13,200/s, 66% of 20,000) and payment calls (926/s, 46%), and sizes gateways, dispatch and geo shards with N+1 zone headroom.

levels.0: REST endpoints for everything, including a location POST every 4 s, with no idempotency.
levels.1: WebSocket for locations and REST for trips, but no sequence numbers, no idempotency keys or no offer endpoints.
levels.2: Unacknowledged location frames with seq; nearby with anonymised IDs and quote; POST /trips with idempotency key returning 202 matching; offer accept/decline with 409 on expiry; guarded lifecycle endpoints; pushes for trip updates.

criteria.title: Two stores for two kinds of truth

levels.0: One database table of drivers updated with every GPS point.
levels.1: Separates positions from trips but keeps assignment state in an eventually consistent or asynchronously replicated store.
levels.2: In-memory geo index (rebuildable, latest-wins) for positions; Postgres with synchronous replica for driver status, trips, offers and outbox; ledger separate; city as the future shard key; explains why neither store can do the other's job.

levels.1: Walks the location update or matching, but not the live trip or payment path.
levels.2: Walks location update (seq check, GEOADD, pub/sub to rider, Kafka), nearby search on replicas, request (auth hold, candidates, ETA matrix, offer, conditional assign), live trip pushes, and completion via outbox to payment, across zone-redundant tiers.

criteria.title: Location ingestion and the live index

levels.0: Writes every update to a relational table with a distance query.
levels.1: Uses an in-memory geo store but no plan for stale drivers, ordering, or sharding hot cities.
levels.2: WebSockets, latest-wins with seq, Redis geo sets per city on primaries with searches on replicas, staleness filter and sweeper, Kafka for history, and a zone-loss timeline with jittered reconnects.

levels.0: Searches only the rider's own cell or computes distance to every driver.
levels.1: Explains geohash prefixes but not the neighbour cells, precision choice or alternatives.
levels.2: Cell plus 8 neighbours with precision chosen from radius, quadtree density adaptation, H3 hexagons for aggregation and surge, widening radius, and ranking by road ETA rather than straight-line distance.

levels.0: Read-then-write assignment, or a lock with no fencing.
levels.1: Uses a conditional update but no reservation during offers, no expiry, or an asynchronously replicated store.
levels.2: Reserve-then-offer compare-and-set with expiry, accept transaction updating driver and trip conditionally, synchronous replication, offer strategy quantified against the 10 s target, and batch matching named as the next step.

criteria.title: Trip state machine and exactly-once charging

levels.0: Free-form status updates and a direct charge call from the API.
levels.1: Has states and an idempotency key at the provider, but a dual write between trip update and payment event, or no reconciliation.
levels.2: Guarded transitions as conditional updates, transactional outbox, idempotent ledger keyed by (trip, kind), provider idempotency keys with retry on timeout, double-entry rows, daily reconciliation, and handling of failed captures.

levels.1: Covers server and zone loss but not provider limits, GPS anomalies or what breaks first at 10×.
levels.2: Zone loss, geo shard and Postgres failover, maps and payment degradation with fallbacks, GPS jumps, reconnect storms; at 10× names the maps quota first, then payments, then sharding Postgres by city and splitting hot cities' geo sets.

levels.1: Generic trade-offs not tied to this design.
levels.2: Each key choice (WebSockets, in-memory index, Postgres for assignment, replica reads, geohash vs H3, ETA ranking, sequential offers, outbox-based payment, city sharding) comes with the alternative and the reason it lost.
